name: Rahambuu
catalog_citation: Mead, David E. 1998. Proto-Bungku-Tolaki: Reconstruction of its phonology and aspects of its morphosyntax. PhD dissertation, Rice University (Rice repository handle 1911/19290), sec. 3.1.2 'Syllable patterns and stress', p. 97. Secondary: Mead, David E. 1999.…
catalog_locator: Mead 1998 sec. 3.1.2 p. 97 (PDF p. 114, scanned of page image); Mead 1999 PL D-91 Appendix 3 p. 101 note (g)
catalog_quote: Mead 1998:96-97, sec. 3.1.2 'Syllable patterns and stress': 'The syllable patterns reconstructed for Proto-Bungku-Tolaki are V(C) and CV(C), with a coda possible only in word-final position—in other words no consonant clusters were possible word-medially. ... I assume that in Proto-Bungku-Tolaki stress fell on the penultimate syllable, there being no reason to reconstruct otherwise. All present-day Bungku-Tolaki languages also exhibit penultimate stress.' Mead 1999:101, Appendix 3 phonemicisation conventions, item (g): 'In the absence of any stress marking, one can assume penultimate stress occurring on the next to last written vowel.' Mead 1999:101-102, 'Important exceptions to phonemicisation', item (d) and following paragraph: 'None of the Bungku-Tolaki languages have phonemically long vowels. Phonetically long vowels are nearly always a reflection of two vowels of the same quality .…

audit.reasoning: Quote check: both deciding quotations (Mead 1998:97 sec. 3.1.2; Mead 1999:101 note (g)) are present verbatim in the held files at the stated locators. The classification (penultimate, fixed) rests on a family-level blanket statement in a 1998 comparative PhD by the sole fieldworker on Rahambuu plus a phonemicisation convention in his 1999 survey; no Rahambuu-specific description of any kind exists (Glottolog: 0 descriptive refs, MED wordlist-or-less), so this is the best available and we hold it. While auditing I scanned sec. 1.5 (printed p. 16) of the same held dissertation and found a sharper statement the record did not cite: 'Stress is penultimate (non-phonemic), with suffixation usually precipitating stress movement.' This confirms the penultimate coding and refines the currently UNSTATED domain field (stress is computed over the suffixed word; 'usually' leaves room for some non-shift
